claude.country: Multinational (39 countries; highest participation from Saudi Arabia, Syria, Egypt, Algeria, Jordan)

links.outcome: Physician test-based clinical competence before vs after AI training course with AI permitted
links.effect: Mean scores rose from 56.88% (SD 15.65) to 77.56% (SD 12.71), pass rate 6.4% to 58.6%, P<.001; no control arm isolating training effect.
links.quote: The mean score improved from 56.88% (SD 15.65%) to 77.56% (SD 12.71%), with a mean difference of 20.68% ( P <.001).

links.outcome: clinical decision-making test performance with generative AI
links.effect: After tailored AI training with GPT-4 use permitted, scores improved from 56.88% to 77.56%, mean difference 20.68%; P<.001.
links.quote: The mean score improved from 56.88% (SD 15.65%) to 77.56% (SD 12.71%), with a mean difference of 20.68% ( P <.001).

links.outcome: physician clinical competence scores and pass rates
links.effect: mean score increased from 56.9% to 77.6% (P<.001) and pass rate from 6.4% to 58.6% (P<.001)
links.quote: The average test scores improved from 56.9% (SD 15.7%) to 77.6% (SD 12.7%; P<.001), and the pass rate increased from 6.4% (21/326) to 58.6% (191/326), with larger gains observed among GPs and younger physicians.
